## Baruch Spinoza quote sources

9 passages attributed to Baruch Spinoza in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Spinoza.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Baruch Spinoza

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

### Sourcing profile

Language of the works

Latin

Cited here from

The Ethics (I, II Prop. 44, III Preface, IV Prop. 67, V Prop. 23 and 42), and the Theological-Political Treatise.

How to cite it

Part, proposition, and scholium — Ethics V, Prop. 42 — because the Ethics is laid out as a geometric demonstration and those divisions are the text's own skeleton. The Tractatus is cited by chapter.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

The Ethics was published posthumously in 1677, in Latin, and Spinoza had suppressed or withheld earlier versions of parts of it for political reasons. Quoting a proposition stripped of its demonstration takes a conclusion out of the argument it was proved from, which in a book built to be proved is a substantial loss.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Where can I check quotations attributed to Baruch Spinoza?

Part, proposition, and scholium — Ethics V, Prop. 42 — because the Ethics is laid out as a geometric demonstration and those divisions are the text's own skeleton. The Tractatus is cited by chapter. This archive cites Baruch Spinoza from The Ethics (I, II Prop. 44, III Preface, IV Prop. 67, V Prop. 23 and 42), and the Theological-Political Treatise. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

#### What is the most common mistake when quoting Baruch Spinoza?

The Ethics was published posthumously in 1677, in Latin, and Spinoza had suppressed or withheld earlier versions of parts of it for political reasons. Quoting a proposition stripped of its demonstration takes a conclusion out of the argument it was proved from, which in a book built to be proved is a substantial loss.

#### What language did Baruch Spinoza write in?

Latin. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
